steps.tx: Autoimmune stimulation of the thyroid gland by agonistic immunoglobulins constitutes the most frequent cause of thyrotoxicosis worldwide. Accounting for sixty to eighty percent of hyperthyroid presentations, **graves disease** occurs predominantly in females between thirty and sixty years of age. Pathophysiology involves the loss of immunological tolerance to the thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor, driving relentless follicular hyperfunction and diffuse glandular hyperplasia. Patients present with classical hypermetabolic features including heat intolerance, fine tremors, sinus tachycardia, unintended weight loss despite increased appetite, and proximal muscle weakness.
steps.say: Autoimmune stimulation of the thyroid gland by agonistic antibodies constitutes the most frequent cause of thyrotoxicosis worldwide. Accounting for sixty to eighty percent of cases, graves disease occurs predominantly in females between thirty and sixty years of age. Patients present with heat intolerance, tremors, sinus tachycardia, weight loss, and proximal myopathy.

steps.tx: Direct binding of circulating autoantibodies to follicular cell membranes stimulates intracellular cyclic adenosine monophosphate cascades independently of pituitary control. Detecting a high circulating **tsh receptor antibody** titre establishes the autoimmune etiology of Graves disease with greater than ninety-five percent sensitivity and specificity. These stimulatory antibodies cross the placental barrier during late pregnancy, creating a significant risk of transient neonatal thyrotoxicosis. Monitoring maternal antibody titres in the third trimester predicts fetal and neonatal risk, while falling titers during antithyroid drug therapy signal disease remission.

left.title: TSH Receptor Antibodies (TRAb / TSI)
points: Pathognomonic stimulatory antibody in Graves disease
Activates TSH receptor, stimulating T3/T4 synthesis
Crosses placenta to cause neonatal hyperthyroidism
High titers indicate severe disease and low remission rate

right.title: Anti-TPO & Anti-Thyroglobulin
points: Destructive cytotoxic antibodies in Hashimoto thyroiditis
Present in 80% of Hashimoto and 50% of Graves
Marker of thyroid autoimmunity, not receptor stimulator

steps.tx: Extrathyroidal manifestations of Graves disease arise from shared antigenic expression and inflammatory cross-talk between orbital fibroblasts and follicular receptors. Progressive proptosis and visual impairment define **exophthalmos**, which occurs in roughly twenty-five to thirty percent of patients. Orbital T-cell infiltration and cytokine activation stimulate preadipocyte differentiation and extensive glycosaminoglycan accumulation, expanding retro-orbital fat and extraocular muscle volume. Patients report grittiness, retrobulbar pressure, and diplopia. Critical complications include exposure keratopathy from incomplete eyelid closure and compressive optic neuropathy, necessitating urgent high-dose intravenous glucocorticoids.
steps.say: Extrathyroidal manifestations of Graves disease arise from shared antigenic expression between orbital fibroblasts and thyroid tissue. Progressive proptosis and visual impairment define exophthalmos, which occurs in thirty percent of patients. Orbital T-cell infiltration stimulates glycosaminoglycan accumulation, expanding retro-orbital fat and muscle volume. Patients experience grittiness, retrobulbar pressure, and diplopia. Severe complications include exposure keratopathy and optic neuropathy, requiring urgent intravenous glucocorticoids.

rows: Prism spectacles or corrective strabismus surgery
Apex crowding by enlarged rectus muscles
Pulse IV methylprednisolone, emergent orbital decompression

steps.tx: Localized autoimmune dermopathy represents a specific and severe extrathyroidal complication occurring almost exclusively in patients with high autoantibody titres. Presenting on the anterior shins, **pretibial myxoedema** manifests as non-pitting, violaceous, indurated plaques with prominent hair follicles creating a peau d orange appearance. Dermal fibroblasts stimulated by local cytokines and TSH receptor antibodies synthesize enormous quantities of hyaluronic acid and chondroitin sulphate, trapping interstitial water. Lesions are typically asymptomatic or mildly pruritic, responding to potent topical corticosteroids applied under occlusive plastic dressings.

Dermal fibroblasts stimulated by cytokines and TSH receptor antibodies produce abundant hyaluronic acid, trapping fluid. steps.tx: Autonomous thyroid nodules functioning independently of pituitary thyroid-stimulating hormone produce non-autoimmune hyperthyroidism in older adults. Commonly complicating long-standing multinodular goitres, **toxic multinodular goitre** (Plummer disease) results from somatic gain-of-function mutations in the TSH receptor gene or the G-protein alpha-subunit. Multiple discrete nodules secrete excess thyroid hormones while normal surrounding parenchyma undergoes atrophy from suppressed pituitary TSH. Patients typically lack infiltrative ophthalmopathy and dermopathy, presenting with insidious cardiovascular manifestations including atrial fibrillation, palpitations, weight loss, and congestive cardiac failure.
steps.say: Autonomous thyroid nodules functioning independently of pituitary thyroid-stimulating hormone produce non-autoimmune hyperthyroidism in older adults. Commonly complicating long-standing goitres, toxic multinodular goitre results from somatic mutations in the TSH receptor gene. Multiple discrete nodules secrete excess thyroid hormones while surrounding parenchyma undergoes functional atrophy. Patients lack ophthalmopathy and dermopathy, presenting with insidious cardiovascular manifestations such as atrial fibrillation and weight loss.

left.title: Toxic Multinodular Goitre
points: Elderly patients with long-standing goitre history
Patchy, heterogeneous tracer uptake on scan
Definitive therapy: Surgery or radioactive iodine

right.title: Toxic Adenoma
points: Solitary hot nodule with suppression of remaining gland
Driven by somatic TSH receptor gain-of-function mutation

steps.tx: A single hyperfunctioning follicular adenoma with somatic receptor mutations produces focal autonomous hormone synthesis. Developing as a solitary **toxic adenoma**, the lesion synthesizes thyroid hormones at high rates, suppressing pituitary thyroid-stimulating hormone secretion to undetectable levels. The absence of endogenous TSH causes functional quiescence and anatomical involution of the normal contralateral thyroid lobe. On examination, a discrete, firm, smooth nodule moves with deglutition without retrosternal extension. It is definitively localized by scintigraphy, which reveals intense isotope concentration within the nodule while the rest of the gland is completely unvisualized.
steps.say: A single hyperfunctioning follicular adenoma with somatic receptor mutations produces focal autonomous hormone synthesis. Developing as a solitary toxic adenoma, the lesion synthesizes thyroid hormones at high rates, suppressing pituitary thyroid-stimulating hormone completely. The absence of endogenous TSH causes functional quiescence of the normal contralateral thyroid lobe. Scintigraphy reveals intense isotope uptake within the nodule, with complete suppression of the remaining gland.

nodes.label: Somatic mutation: TSH receptor or Gs-alpha gain-of-function
Hypersecretion: High T3/T4 suppresses pituitary TSH to < 0.01
Contralateral lobe: Complete quiescence and isotope non-visualization

steps.tx: Quantitative functional imaging provides the definitive physiological separation between high-uptake hyperthyroidism and destructive low-uptake thyrotoxic disorders. Performing **radioactive iodine uptake** (RAIU) using iodine-123 or technetium-99m measures the percentage of administered tracer trapped by follicular cells over twenty-four hours. True endogenous hyperthyroidism demonstrates elevated uptake: Graves disease exhibits high diffuse symmetrical uptake, toxic multinodular goitre shows patchy heterogeneous uptake, and toxic adenoma demonstrates a focal hot nodule. Conversely, subacute thyroiditis, factitious thyroid hormone ingestion, and struma ovarii show low or absent uptake under two percent.
steps.say: Quantitative functional imaging provides physiological separation between high-uptake hyperthyroidism and destructive low-uptake thyrotoxic disorders. Performing radioactive iodine uptake using iodine-123 measures the percentage of tracer trapped by follicular cells over twenty-four hours. True hyperthyroidism demonstrates elevated uptake: Graves exhibits high diffuse uptake, toxic multinodular goitre shows patchy uptake, and toxic adenoma shows a solitary hot nodule. Conversely, subacute thyroiditis and factitious ingestion show negligible uptake.

steps.tx: Definitive long-term treatment strategies balance medical thionamide control, radioiodine ablation, and surgical thyroidectomy. While antithyroid medications serve as initial therapy in Graves disease, **radioactive iodine** ablation using iodine-131 destroys hyperfunctioning follicular cells over six to twelve weeks. Radioiodine is contraindicated during pregnancy, lactation, and in active moderate-to-severe Graves ophthalmopathy because post-ablative antigen release can exacerbate orbital inflammation. Total or near-total thyroidectomy provides rapid cure for large goitres with compressive symptoms, suspicion of malignancy, or patient choice, requiring lifelong postoperative levothyroxine replacement.
